name: GitHub
summary: Turns your GitHub notifications into FocusDeck signals: review requests, finished CI and agent runs, and everything else.
description: A small poller reads your GitHub notifications once a minute through your own GitHub CLI login. A pull request review or deployment approval waiting on you opens a loop. A finished workflow run or Copilot cloud agent session counts as an agent finishing. Every other new notification is a notification. Each event carries only its kind and an opaque hash of the notification thread; titles, repositories, people and URLs never leave your machine.

emits.when: Someone requests your review on a pull request, or your approval for a deployment
A workflow run you triggered completes, or a Copilot cloud agent session finishes

neverSends: Who did what: authors, commenters and reviewers

setup.title: Log in to the GitHub CLI
setup.body: The poller reads your notifications through gh, as you. gh's own login includes the repo scope the notifications API needs; fine-grained personal access tokens can't read notifications.

code.content:
gh auth login
gh auth status

setup.title: Start the poller
setup.body: It polls once a minute until you stop it with Ctrl-C. Its first poll only remembers the notifications already there, so your backlog isn't replayed. If FocusDeck has a sensor token, set FOCUSDECK_SENSOR_TOKEN as well. To keep it running in the background, see the docs for systemd and launchd examples.

setup.title: Designate GitHub in FocusDeck
setup.body: Until GitHub is designated, the bridge drops its events.

test.expect: The terminal prints "focusdeck-github: sent" with status 200, and FocusDeck shows a GitHub notification once GitHub is designated. It doesn't call gh.
